subject: Post-call: paperwork path & pricing options — next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha@cleardata.io>; Procurement Team <procurement@cleardata.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: paperwork path & pricing options — next steps

Thanks again for taking the time this morning, Aisha — good discussion. Below is a concise recap and the asks we agreed on so your procurement and finance teams can triage next:

Summary of outcomes from call:
- ClearData is leaning toward a PO-based purchase for budget control but is open to marketplace procurement if it shortens approval cycles.
- Primary use: customer-facing document generation (PII-sanitized); data residency to remain in us-west region.
- Preference: start on hosted API for fast time-to-value, evaluate Dedicated for steady throughput in Q4. Private (on-prem/VPC) mentioned as a future need for regulated customers.

Open questions / asks for procurement:
1) Please confirm preferred purchasing mechanism: PO (net-30), corporate card, or marketplace listing.
2) If PO: who is the procurement contact (name + email) and any required PO language/clauses?
3) If marketplace: which marketplace (AWS, Azure) and do you require marketplace billing vs direct Redwoods invoice?
4) Timing: desired contract execution date and required internal approvals.

Pricing/packaging note (high level):
- Hosted (on-demand): no commit, per-token billing, fastest start.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): commit pricing with monthly/annual minimums; significant unit-cost reduction at predictable throughput.
- Private: license + support; typically longer procurement windows.

Next steps (we proposed):
- Aisha to confirm purchasing mechanism and introduce procurement contact by COB 6/22.
- Redwood to send a short Commercial Summary (pricing ranges, commit thresholds) + SOW template and a TCO spreadsheet for Dedicated vs Private.
- Optional: 30-minute procurement Q&A with our finance team this week if helpful.

Attachments: Redwood_COMMS_Summary.pdf (short pricing ranges), Dedicated_vs_Private_TCO.xlsx, SOW_template.docx

Thanks — I’ll follow up with formal summary + links once procurement contact is looped in.

Best,
Priyom
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Aisha / Michael — looping in a quick commercial breakdown so procurement has the concrete numbers for comparison. High level answers below and I attached the TCO workbook + SOW template.

Committed vs on-demand (simplified):
- Hosted (on-demand): pay-as-you-go; no minimums; good for PoC and initial months; unit price = list_hosted_unit_rate.
- Dedicated (reserved): minimum commit typically starts at $25k/month (3-month minimum for pilots we sometimes accept) with steeper discounts at 6/12 month commitments. Example: 12-month commit at 80% utilization yields ~45% unit reduction vs hosted. Exact numbers tailored to model + token profile.
- Private deployment: one-time platform fee + annual support; procurement cadence longer due to infra/hosting approvals.

Marketplace notes:
- Marketplace purchases (AWS/Azure) typically use marketplace billing rules which can limit committed pricing flexibility. In those cases we can offer equivalent pricing via direct PO (and pass marketplace incentives where possible). We'll flag any marketplace-specific constraints in the formal quote.

Procurement materials attached: Redwood_COMMS_Summary.pdf, Dedicated_vs_Private_TCO.xlsx, SOW_template.docx

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood to issue an initial quote (range) for a PO path by 6/23.
2) Procurement Q&A: propose 30-min call Tues 6/24 at 10:00am PT — please confirm availability.
3) If PO is confirmed, Michael can send a sample PO template or standard terms to speed redlines.

If useful I can include an explicit line-item mapping (hosted tokens vs dedicated nodes) for your FinOps team prior to the quote.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi Aisha / Michael — Ben from Solutions Engineering here. Adding a couple technical clarifications ahead of procurement review. Forwarding Lauren's note below for context.

Key technical notes:
- Data residency: hosted in us-west is supported; we can bind customer projects to a region and provide audit logs for access.
- Dedicated sizing: we size based on peak concurrent requests and token profile. For initial sizing we can assume X tokens/session and Y concurrent sessions — we’ll provide a recommended node footprint in the formal SOW.
- Security/compliance: Redwood supports SOC 2 Type II; we can provide the attestation and a redacted security package for vendor management.
